highlights: BVerfG 2 BvR 226/26: Court must not arbitrarily dismiss factual claims — E-Bike case shows prohibition of objective arbitrariness in civil litigation (Art. 3(1) GG)
EuGH C-526/24: Single GDPR access request can be abusive if filed not to learn about processing but to manufacture damages claims; good-faith requests remain protected
EuGH C-26/25 Bukla: Return bans based on classified intelligence must not break up EU-citizen families; authorities must show essential reasons and examine individual circumstances

toolnotes.agb-reader: No direct impact on AGB clause checks; ruling is about constitutional procedural fairness.
toolnotes.flight-rights-mcp: No direct EU261 impact; Bukla case relates to immigration/expulsion and family life, relevant context for mobility rights.
toolnotes.gitlaw: C-526/24 is relevant for legal-tech jurisprudence on GDPR access rights and abuse; consider noting the new abuse standard in any DSGVO briefing tools.
